faq: What counts as a lapsed customer?
It depends on how often your buyers usually reorder. We look at your order history to set the right number of days, and you can change it later in the flow settings.
Is it a problem to email people who stopped opening?
Emailing very cold contacts can hurt delivery. Our flow ends with a stay or leave email and then stops sending to those who do not respond, which keeps your list healthy.
Do I need to offer a discount?
Not always. A genuine reminder or a new product can be enough, and we write it that way if you prefer. When margins allow, a modest offer in the last message is a common choice.
Can the flow also help with subscribers who never bought?
Not this flow. It is built for past buyers. People who never ordered need a different message, and our welcome flow service covers them, so we do not mix the two.

desc:
A win-back email flow for lapsed customers reaches people who bought once and then went quiet. Ecom Swift LLC builds it in your own email tool: a friendly check-in, a reminder of what they liked and a final message that asks them to stay or go.

## What is a win-back flow?

A win-back flow is an automated series sent to customers who have not purchased for longer than is normal for your business. The tool watches the date of each customer's last order. When that gap passes a set point, the person enters the flow and receives a short sequence of messages.

If they buy again, they leave the flow at once. If they ignore every message, they can be removed from regular sending.

## Why lapsed customers deserve their own message

A returning customer already knows your brand, so reaching them is usually easier than finding a stranger. But the usual newsletter is the wrong tool. It speaks to everyone and says nothing about the gap. A message that notices the person has been away, mentions what they bought and gives a reason to look again feels more human.

There is a second benefit. Contacts who never respond hurt your sending reputation, because mail providers read disengagement as a sign that your messages are unwanted. A final "do you want to stay?" message lets interested people say yes and lets others leave cleanly, which keeps your list healthier. Results depend on your products, buying cycle and how long customers have been away.

## What a good win-back program includes

- A definition of "lapsed" that fits your products, such as a gap longer than your usual reorder time.
- A trigger based on the date of the last order.
- Exclusion of anyone who has bought recently.
- A first message that is warm and personal, without guilt.
- A reminder of the last purchased product or related items.
- An optional comeback offer, only if it suits your margins.
- A feedback survey email asking why they left, if you want answers.
- A final message asking people to stay on the list or be removed.
- Automatic removal or suppression of people who never respond.
- A text step for customers who opted in to SMS.

## How we set it up

We first check how often your customers usually reorder, because a lapsed customer for a candle store differs from one for a mattress seller. Then we choose the timing windows, write the messages and build the flow in your tool with the right filters. We test it with a sample customer profile to make sure it starts, stops and removes people as intended.

The Basic package delivers three win-back emails for past buyers, with the last message asking to stay on the list. Standard adds an SMS step, the last purchased product, two timing windows and automatic removal of non-responders. Premium adds windows by customer value, a survey email, a subject line test and a results guide with a handover call. Add-ons include an extra reminder email, a feedback survey page and a return path for your best customers. Only past buyers enter the flow.

## Do and avoid

**Do:**
- Match the gap to your normal buying rhythm.
- Remind people of something they actually bought.
- Make staying and leaving equally easy.
- Remove people who never respond.
- Watch replies, because some lapsed customers have questions.

**Avoid:**
- Treating every old contact as a customer.
- Opening with guilt or pressure.
- Giving the biggest offer in the first message.
- Mailing people who recently ordered.
- Keeping unresponsive contacts forever.

## Who it suits

A store with many one-time buyers has the most to gain. A subscription or consumable brand can catch customers who stopped reordering. A business planning a big campaign can clean its list first so the send reaches people who want it.

## What we need from you

Tell us your store platform, email or SMS tool and how long customers typically wait between orders. Share brand assets, tone notes and any offer limits. We never need passwords. Access is given as a collaborator, staff or team user where the tool allows it, and you remain the owner of all accounts.
